title: Advanced Use of “y” & “en”
description: Pronoun order and idioms built on y and en.

items.explain: Tu t'y prends mal. — You are going about it the wrong way.

items.prompt: In French: “to get used to it”
items.explain: C'est dur au début, mais on s'y fait. — It is hard at first, but you get used to it.
Tout le monde est venu, y compris Paul. — Everyone came, including Paul.

options: to be attached to it / to insist
to be exhausted / unable to take any more
items.answer: to be attached to it / to insist
items.explain: Cette montre ? J'y tiens beaucoup. — This watch? I am very attached to it.

items.exampleEn: I am still angry with him.

items.explain: Ne t'en fais pas ! — Don't worry!

items.prompt: In French: “to be exhausted / unable to take any more”
items.explain: Je n'en peux plus. — I can't take any more.

items.exampleFr: J'en ai assez de ce bruit.
items.exampleEn: I have had enough of this noise.

items.explain: Je m'en fiche complètement. — I couldn't care less.

items.prompt: What does “y être pour quelque chose” mean?
options: to have something to do with it
items.answer: to have something to do with it
items.explain: Je n'y suis pour rien. — I have nothing to do with it.

items.translation: me, te, se, nous, vous → le, la, les → lui, leur → y → en
items.exampleFr: Je lui en donne. Il les y met. Il y en a trois.
items.exampleEn: I give him some. He puts them there. There are three of them.

items.prompt: Replace both nouns: “Je donne du pain à Paul.”
Replace both nouns: “Il met les clés dans le sac.”
Replace both nouns: “Parle de ce problème à ta mère !”
Replace the place: “Va à la boulangerie !”
items.explain: The -s returns before y for pronunciation.

items.prompt: Replace both nouns: “Elle envoie des fleurs à ses parents.”
